subject: mathematics
title: Equivalent fractions
summary: You will be able to make equivalent fractions, simplify a fraction to its lowest terms using the HCF, and compare and order fractions.
objectives: Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same number
Simplify fractions to their lowest terms using the highest common factor (HCF)
Compare two fractions using a common denominator
Arrange a set of fractions in ascending or descending order

sections.title: Who ate more bread?
sections.body:
Mutale and Joseph each buy the same size of loaf in Ndola. Mutale cuts hers into 2 equal pieces and eats 1 piece: 1/2. Joseph cuts his into 4 equal pieces and eats 2 pieces: 2/4. Who ate more?

They ate exactly the same amount. 1/2 and 2/4 look different, but they show the same part of the whole. Fractions like this are called equivalent fractions. Equivalent means "equal in value".

sections.title: Making equivalent fractions
sections.body:
To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number (not 0). You are cutting every piece into smaller equal pieces, so the amount does not change.

You can also divide the numerator and denominator by the same number, as long as both divide exactly.

sections.title: Worked example: finding a missing number
steps: Step 1: Look at the denominators. What turns 5 into 20? 20 ÷ 5 = 4, so the denominator was multiplied by 4.
Step 2: Do the same to the numerator: 3 × 4 = 12.
Step 3: Check: 12/20 divided top and bottom by 4 gives 3/5 again.

sections.question: Which fraction is NOT equivalent to 2/3?
sections.explanation: 4/6, 8/12 and 10/15 come from multiplying 2 and 3 by 2, 4 and 5. 5/6 comes from adding 3 to the top and bottom, which does not keep the value: 5/6 is bigger than 2/3. Only multiplying or dividing works.

sections.title: Simplifying to lowest terms
sections.body:
To simplify a fraction means to write it with the smallest possible numbers. A fraction is in its lowest terms when the only number that divides both the numerator and the denominator exactly is 1.

The quickest way is to divide both numbers by their highest common factor (HCF). A factor is a number that divides exactly into another number. The HCF is the biggest factor that two numbers share.

sections.title: Worked example: simplifying with the HCF
steps: Step 3: The highest factor in both lists is 12, so the HCF is 12.
Step 4: Divide top and bottom by 12: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3.
Step 5: 2 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so 2/3 is in lowest terms.

sections.title: Common mistake: adding instead of multiplying, or stopping too early
sections.body:
Some learners think that adding the same number to the top and bottom gives an equivalent fraction. It does not. Adding 1 to the top and bottom of 1/2 gives 2/3, but 2/3 is bigger than 1/2. Always multiply or divide.

Another mistake is stopping before the fraction is fully simplified. 12/18 ÷ 2 gives 6/9, but 6 and 9 can still both be divided by 3, giving 2/3. Using the HCF in one step avoids this. Always check if the new numbers share a factor.

sections.title: Comparing fractions
sections.body:
If two fractions have the same denominator, the one with the bigger numerator is bigger: 5/8 > 3/8. If they have the same numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is bigger: 1/3 > 1/5, because thirds are bigger pieces than fifths.

If both numbers are different, change them to equivalent fractions with a common denominator (the same denominator). The best choice is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of the denominators: the smallest number that both denominators divide into exactly.

sections.title: Worked example: which is bigger?
steps: Step 1: Find the LCM of 4 and 7. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28. Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28. The LCM is 28.

sections.question: Which is larger, 5/8 or 2/3?
sections.explanation: The LCM of 8 and 3 is 24. 5/8 = 15/24 and 2/3 = 16/24. Since 16 > 15, 2/3 is larger. Do not just compare the 5 and the 2 on top: the pieces are different sizes until the denominators match.

sections.title: Worked example: putting fractions in order
sections.problem: Arrange 2/3, 1/2, 5/6 and 3/4 in ascending order (smallest first).
steps: Step 1: The denominators are 3, 2, 6 and 4. Their LCM is 12.
Step 3: Order the numerators from smallest: 6, 8, 9, 10.
Step 4: Write the original fractions in that order.

sections.title: Key points
bullets: Equivalent fractions have the same value, for example 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
Make equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number. Never add or subtract.
Simplify to lowest terms by dividing the top and bottom by their HCF.
To compare or order fractions, change them to a common denominator, best the LCM of the denominators.
With the same denominator, the bigger numerator means the bigger fraction.

quiz.question: Equivalent fractions are fractions that...
quiz.explanation: Equivalent means equal in value. 1/2 and 3/6 have different numerators and denominators but show the same amount, so they are equivalent.

quiz.question: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 16 and 24?
quiz.explanation: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The biggest number in both lists is 8. 4 and 2 are common factors but not the highest. 48 is a common multiple, not a factor.

quiz.question: Simplify 18/24 to its lowest terms.
quiz.explanation: The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4, giving 3/4. 9/12 and 6/8 are equivalent to 3/4 but are not in lowest terms, because they can still be divided.

quiz.question: Find the missing number: 4/7 = ?/35
quiz.explanation: 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so the denominator was multiplied by 5. Multiply the numerator by 5 too: 4 × 5 = 20. The answer 32 comes from adding 28 to the top, as 28 was added to the bottom; adding does not keep the value.

quiz.question: Which fraction is already in its lowest terms?
quiz.explanation: The factors of 7 are 1 and 7, and 7 does not divide 12. So 7 and 12 share only the factor 1, and 7/12 cannot be simplified. 6/9 = 2/3, 10/15 = 2/3 and 4/8 = 1/2 can all be simplified.

quiz.question: Which is greater, 3/5 or 4/7?
quiz.explanation: The LCM of 5 and 7 is 35. 3/5 = 21/35 and 4/7 = 20/35. 21 > 20, so 3/5 is greater. Any two fractions can be compared once they have a common denominator.

quiz.question: Arrange 1/2, 5/12 and 2/3 in ascending order (smallest first).
quiz.explanation: Use the common denominator 12: 1/2 = 6/12, 5/12 stays 5/12, 2/3 = 8/12. Ordering 5, 6, 8 gives 5/12, 1/2, 2/3. The order 2/3, 1/2, 5/12 is descending (largest first), not ascending.

quiz.question: Mwansa scored 15 out of 20 in a Science test. Chileshe scored 18 out of 25. Who did better?
quiz.explanation: Compare 15/20 and 18/25. The LCM of 20 and 25 is 100. 15/20 = 75/100 and 18/25 = 72/100. 75 > 72, so Mwansa did better. Chileshe got more marks (18), but out of a bigger total, so marks alone do not decide it.

glossary.definition: Fractions that look different but have the same value, for example 1/2 and 3/6.
To write a fraction using smaller numbers without changing its value, by dividing the top and bottom by the same number.
A fraction is in lowest terms when its numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1, for example 2/3.
A whole number that divides exactly into another number. 3 is a factor of 12.
The biggest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6.
The smallest number that two or more numbers all divide into exactly. The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12.
The same denominator shared by two or more fractions, so that they can be compared, added or subtracted.
